text:
maya: Heads up — after the EU egress policy change this morning we're seeing a spike in NAT GW metrics and a pile of keystore decrypt errors on new GPU nodes. Provisioning is stalling during init.

josh: Saw that too. metrics: natgw_conn_count jumped ~4x around 08:12 UTC. GPU warm pool nodes failing to call keystore with 403-ish errors.

priya: Is this the split-egress rule that routes S3 and KMS via privatelink except for controlplane? Could be a path mismatch to the keystore proxy.

maya: Exactly. We changed the egress ACL to prefer privatelink for data plane and default to natgw for controlplane. It looks like the keystore agent is resolving keystore.<region>.internal -> private IP sometimes and public other times. Mix is causing return-path asymmetry.

ben: Repro steps I ran on a staging node: 
```
curl -v https://keystore.eu.internal/health
# got TCP RST intermittently
traceroute keystore.eu.internal
# shows hop to privatelink then nth hop to natgw
```

priya: That asymmetry will trigger our firewall stateful inspection to drop packets. Also flow logs are exploding — audit retention will cost us if we keep this volume.

secops-bot: Audit alert: vpc_flow_logs volume increased 3.8x in eu-west-1 between 08:10 and 08:20 UTC. Estimated incremental cost: $1.2k/day if sustained.

josh: Short-term mitigation: revert the split policy and pin keystore traffic to privatelink-only, or flip to natgw-only for now. Which is faster?

maya: Revert to natgw-only is quickest (just revert ACL rule set). But that sacrifices privatelink isolation for S3 --> increase blast radius. Privatelink-only is more config work (route table changes + make sure keystore DNS resolves private IP consistently).

priya: We should avoid long-lived revert. Proposed plan: 1) revert to natgw-only for next 30m to unstuck provisioning, 2) enable VPC flow log sampling (1%) to curb audit cost, 3) schedule a follow-up to hard-pin keystore DNS via Route53 private records + healthchecks so path stays consistent.

ben: I can do step 1 now. Reverting ACL in eu-west-1 and will watch provisioning.

secops-bot: Change request created: CR-2026-1173 by ben. Auto-notify on completion.

josh: For the longer-term we also need an IAM tweak: agent role should be allowed to call kms:Decrypt only via keystore proxy principal to avoid bypass if public path resumes. That reduces risk.

priya: Agreed. Also add a keystore-side check to reject requests that don't come from the privatelink subnet CIDR. Adds defense-in-depth.

maya: Ben — after revert can you bump warm pool size by +15 nodes temporarily so we can clear the backlog? We'll scale down after validation.

ben: Revert complete at 08:28 UTC. Warm pool +15 queued. Monitoring now.

maya: Provisioning cleared for ~40% of stuck instances. Still seeing a handful retrying with keystore timeouts.

priya: I'll open a runbook PR with DNS hard-pin steps and include terraform snippet for Route53 private record and healthcheck. Also will add flow log sampling toggle script.

josh: Thx. For cost planning: secops, can you put an alert if vpc_flow_logs > 2x baseline for >10m? We'll need to be notified before bill surprises.

secops-bot: Alert rule updated: vpc_flow_logs_rate_threshold in eu-west-1 set to 2.0x baseline, window 10m.

maya: Next steps summary: 1) Priya will author Route53 + keystore hard-pin PR, 2) Josh will propose IAM role restriction for agent->keystore KMS calls, 3) Ben will monitor warm pool and scale down after backlog cleared, 4) Secops to monitor flow log alerting and cost.

priya: Will do PR and tag @josh @maya for review.

ben: Warm pool scaled back at 09:05 UTC, backlog cleared. Provisioning success rate back to normal.

maya: Thanks team — good catch on the asymmetry. We'll treat this as a post-change checklist item: DNS pin + flow-log sampling + rollout canary. :thumbsup:

josh: I'll add the checklist to the infra playbook and link to the CR.

secops-bot: Incident closed by maya. Root cause: egress path asymmetry from split-egress policy.

maya: Filing a short postmortem doc now with cost delta and actionable follow-ups.
